slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
The angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to a line of sight. The angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal.

The angle of depression from A to B equals the angle of elevation from B to A: the two horizontals are parallel, so they are alternate interior angles.

Example: from 30 m away, the top of a tree is at an elevation of 40 degrees from eye level 1.5 m above the ground. The tree is 1.5 + 30 tan 40 degrees, about 1.5 + 25.2 = 26.7 m tall.
